lead: A three-phase supply is three sine voltages of equal RMS magnitude and frequency, displaced by 120°. One rotating field in a generator produces all three at once. Industry uses it because three-phase motors turn smoothly, cables carry less current for the same power, and a star winding gives two voltage levels. In a star connection the three winding ends meet at a neutral point. In a delta connection they form a closed loop with no neutral. The names to keep straight are phase voltage, line voltage, phase current and line current; each connection fixes which pairs are equal.
prereq: You need: phasors for 120° displacement and complex impedance for the worked example.

sections.h3: Three voltages from one rotating field

blocks.text: A three-phase generator has three identical windings A, B and C on the stator, spaced 120 electrical degrees apart. The rotor field sweeps past them in turn. Each winding gets an emf of the same peak and frequency. The emfs reach their peaks in a fixed order called the phase sequence, written R-Y-B or A-B-C. Reversing any two lines reverses the sequence and reverses a three-phase motor.
v<sub>A</sub> = V<sub>m</sub> sin(ωt), v<sub>B</sub> = V<sub>m</sub> sin(ωt − 120°), v<sub>C</sub> = V<sub>m</sub> sin(ωt + 120°)
blocks.where: V<sub>m</sub> is peak voltage in V; ω = 2πf is angular frequency in rad/s; f is frequency in Hz; t is time in s; the three voltages have equal V<sub>m</sub> and f.

blocks.text: The three voltages sum to zero at every instant in a balanced set. That is why a three-wire system can work without a return wire for balanced loads. The four quantities used from here on are: phase voltage V<sub>ph</sub>, the voltage across one phase winding; line voltage V<sub>L</sub>, the voltage between two line conductors; phase current I<sub>ph</sub>, the current through one winding; and line current I<sub>L</sub>, the current in one line conductor. A balanced load has equal impedances in all three phases, so the three phase currents also have equal magnitude and are 120° apart.

The exact √3 relations between line and phase quantities are derived in Chapter 2.7. Here keep the equalities straight for each connection. Phase sequence and balanced phasors use the ideas from Chapter 2.3.

sections.h3: Star connection: a neutral point appears

blocks.text: Join one end of each winding A, B and C to a common point N. Leave the other ends as the three line terminals. This is the star or Y connection. Point N is the neutral point. Figure 1 shows the star on the left. The neutral wire, when brought out, is the fourth wire of a four-wire star system.

items: Line current equals phase current: I<sub>L</sub> = I<sub>ph</sub>. The same current flows from the line into a winding.
Line voltage is not equal to phase voltage. In a balanced star, V<sub>L</sub> is larger than V<sub>ph</sub>; the √3 factor is proved in Chapter 2.7.
Two voltage levels are available: V<sub>L</sub> between any two lines and V<sub>ph</sub> between one line and neutral. A 400 V line-to-line star supply gives about 230 V line-to-neutral.
The neutral carries the return current of unbalanced loads. In a balanced star load, the three equal phase currents are 120° apart, so their sum is zero and neutral current is zero.

blocks.text: Domestic single-phase 230 V in India is one line and neutral of a 400 V star distribution. The same star winding also feeds three-phase motors at 400 V. The neutral point is often earthed for safety; earthing practice belongs to Unit 6.

sections.h3: Delta connection: a closed three-wire loop

blocks.text: Connect the end of winding A to the start of winding B, the end of B to the start of C, and the end of C back to the start of A. The three windings form a closed triangle. This is the delta or mesh connection. The three corners are the line terminals D1, D2 and D3 in Figure 1. There is no neutral point and no fourth wire.

items: Line voltage equals phase voltage: V<sub>L</sub> = V<sub>ph</sub>. Each pair of lines is connected directly across one winding.
Line current is not equal to phase current. Each line current is the phasor difference of the two winding currents at that corner; the √3 relation for a balanced delta is in Chapter 2.7.
The closed loop has no neutral. Never connect a neutral wire to a delta load: there is no neutral terminal, and forcing one can unbalance the winding voltages.
In a balanced set the three emfs sum to zero, so no circulating current flows around the closed triangle. Slight unbalance can cause a small circulating current.

blocks.text: Delta is common for three-phase motors and for transformer windings where a neutral is not needed. Some syllabi call star the Y connection and delta the mesh connection; both names describe the same drawings.

figure.caption: Left: A, B and C meet at neutral N to form a star. Right: D1, D2 and D3 form a closed delta loop with no neutral point.

spec.aria: Left side shows a star connection with a neutral point; right side shows a closed delta loop with no neutral.

examples.question: A balanced 400 V line-to-line, 50 Hz supply feeds a star-connected load with per-phase impedance Z = 20∠30° Ω. Find the phase voltage, the phase current magnitude and the line current magnitude. State the phase angle of the current relative to the phase voltage.
steps: Connection is star. Given line voltage V<sub>L</sub> = 400 V and per-phase impedance magnitude |Z| = 20 Ω with angle +30°.
In star the phase voltage is line-to-neutral: V<sub>ph</sub> = V<sub>L</sub> / √3 = 400 / 1.732 = 230.9 V.
Phase current magnitude: I<sub>ph</sub> = V<sub>ph</sub> / |Z| = 230.9 / 20 = 11.55 A.
The impedance angle is +30°, so the current lags the phase voltage by 30°.
In star, line current equals phase current: I<sub>L</sub> = I<sub>ph</sub> = 11.55 A.
examples.answer: The phase voltage is 230.9 V; the phase current and line current are 11.55 A each, and the current lags the phase voltage by 30°.
examples.check:
import math
VL = 400.0
Zmag = 20.0
angle_deg = 30.0
Vph = VL/math.sqrt(3)
Iph = Vph/Zmag
IL = Iph
print(round(Vph, 1))
print(round(Iph, 2))
print(round(IL, 2))
print(round(angle_deg, 1))

traps: Line voltage is between two lines; phase voltage is across one phase winding. A 400 V three-phase label normally means line-to-line, not 400 V per phase.
In star, line current equals phase current; in delta, line voltage equals phase voltage. Do not mix the two equalities.
Delta has no neutral point. Never connect a neutral wire to a delta load; there is no fourth terminal to take it.
Phase sequence matters. Swapping any two lines reverses R-Y-B to R-B-Y and reverses a three-phase motor.
Do not use 400/√3 for a delta load. The √3 factor belongs to balanced star line voltage, not to every three-phase circuit.

quiz.a: The order in which the three phase voltages reach their positive peaks, such as R-Y-B or A-B-C.

quiz.q: Why does a star connection offer two voltage levels?
quiz.a: The neutral point gives a line-to-neutral voltage V<sub>ph</sub>, while two line terminals give a line-to-line voltage V<sub>L</sub>. In a balanced star, V<sub>L</sub> is larger than V<sub>ph</sub>.

quiz.q: A balanced 415 V line-to-line star load has per-phase impedance magnitude 10 Ω. Find the phase voltage and line current magnitude.
quiz.a: V<sub>ph</sub> = 415/√3 = 239.6 V. I<sub>ph</sub> = 239.6/10 = 23.96 A. In star, I<sub>L</sub> = I<sub>ph</sub> = 23.96 A.

quiz.q: A delta load has no neutral. What happens if a technician connects the supply neutral to one delta corner?
quiz.a: There is no neutral terminal. Connecting the supply neutral to one corner can force that corner to neutral potential, unbalance the three winding voltages and cause large currents; it is a fault.

quiz.q: In a delta-connected load, line voltage is 400 V and phase impedance magnitude is 20 Ω. Find the phase current magnitude.
quiz.a: In delta, V<sub>ph</sub> = V<sub>L</sub> = 400 V. I<sub>ph</sub> = 400/20 = 20 A. The line current needs the √3 relation, which is not asked here.

quiz.q: Why is the neutral current zero in a balanced star load?
quiz.a: The three phase currents have equal magnitude and are 120° apart. Their phasor sum is zero, so no current returns through the neutral.

quiz.q: A motor nameplate says 400 V, 50 Hz, delta. Why should you not assume its phase voltage is 230 V?
quiz.a: In delta, line voltage equals phase voltage, so each winding sees 400 V. The 230 V value is the line-to-neutral voltage of a 400 V star system, not a delta winding.

quiz.q: Define line current and phase current.
quiz.a: Line current is the current in one line conductor. Phase current is the current through one phase winding.

beyond: Not for the exam. Grid operators keep phase sequence and phase angle tight because paralleling generators needs matching voltage, frequency and sequence. Delta windings block zero-sequence current from the line side, so protection relays watch circulating current. Power-electronics converters now synthesise three-phase voltages from DC, and phase-locked loops track the grid angle. Search terms: phase sequence indicator, open-delta, zero-sequence, dq transformation.
